key_insight: HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC produced the most oxidation-resistant coating on SA516 steel, sharply reducing high-temperature mass gain by forming a dense protective oxide scale.
engineering_relevance: For boiler and high-temperature service components, selecting HVOF-sprayed Ni-Cr ceramic composite coatings can greatly improve cyclic oxidation life and delay spallation.
method: Compared uncoated SA516 steel with Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings applied by HVOF and plasma spray.
Ran cyclic air oxidation tests for 50 cycles at 900°C.
Characterized phases and microstructure using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating showed the best performance, reducing maximum weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 steel.
watch_item: Results are based on laboratory cyclic oxidation at 900°C, so field performance may differ under thermal shock, corrosion mixtures, or long-term service conditions.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
